caption: "duncan sheik" — 200,000+ searches this week. Swipe for 10 things most people don't know about the man behind Barely Breathing and Spring Awakening.
Why: Duncan Sheik died on September 17 in New York at 56. His mother told The New York Times the cause was cardiac arrest. His family will not share more.

What most people don't know: Barely Breathing only reached number 16, yet it stayed on the Billboard Hot 100 for 55 straight weeks. Ten years later he wrote the music for Spring Awakening, built on an 1891 German play; it won eight Tonys and launched Lea Michele and Jonathan Groff.
Very simply put: one song stayed 55 weeks. One musical won eight Tonys.

slides.headline: He died September 17 in New York, aged *56*.
slides.sub: Cardiac arrest, his mother told The New York Times. His family will not share more medical details.

slides.headline: Barely Breathing peaked at 16 and stayed *55 weeks*.
slides.sub: Fifty-five consecutive weeks on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1996 and 1997. The debut album went gold.
slides.image: A vinyl record on a turntable in warm afternoon light, record in the upper half of the frame, lower half plain wooden shelf, photorealistic, no readable labels, no text

slides.headline: He studied *semiotics* at Brown.
slides.sub: Phillips Academy Andover, class of 1988; Brown University, class of 1992.
slides.image: A stack of old hardcover books on a library desk under a green lamp, books in the upper half of the frame, lower half plain dark wood, photorealistic, no readable text

slides.headline: Ten years after the hit, he wrote *Spring Awakening*.
slides.sub: Music by Sheik, book and lyrics by Steven Sater. Off-Broadway May 19, 2006; Broadway December 10, 2006.
slides.image: Handwritten sheet music pages spread on a piano under a spotlight, pages in the upper half of the frame, lower half plain black piano, photorealistic, no readable text

slides.headline: The musical is built on a German play from *1891*.
slides.sub: Frank Wedekind's play of the same name, written 115 years before the musical opened.
slides.image: A worn leather-bound antique book open on a dark desk beside a quill, book in the upper half of the frame, lower half plain dark wood, photorealistic, no readable text

slides.headline: It won *eight Tonys*, two of them his.
slides.sub: Best Musical, Best Original Score with Sater, Best Orchestrations for Sheik, in 2007. The cast album won a Grammy in 2008.
slides.image: A row of silver award statuettes on a dark shelf under a spotlight, statuettes in the upper half of the frame, lower half plain dark shelf, photorealistic, no text, no logos

slides.headline: The original cast had *Lea Michele* and Jonathan Groff.
slides.sub: John Gallagher Jr. won a Tony for it. The show ran 859 performances, closing January 18, 2009.
slides.image: Empty red velvet theatre seats facing a lit stage with the curtain down, seats in the upper half of the frame, lower half plain dark floor, photorealistic, no people, no text

slides.headline: He turned *American Psycho* into a musical.
slides.sub: London's Almeida in 2013, Broadway in 2016. Nine studio albums, the last in 2022. A practising Nichiren Buddhist.
slides.image: A lit theatre marquee at night with blank white panels, marquee in the upper half of the frame, lower half plain wet street, photorealistic, no text

slides.headline: Very simply put: 55 weeks on the chart, then *eight Tonys*.
